newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares at record high on speculative buys.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares at record high on speculative buys.

text.p: Turkey's stock market index hit a record high on Thursday as speculative buying buoyed a recent uptrend after a period of weakness when political uncertainty hampered the market, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 index ended morning trading 2.35 percent higher at 75,584.08, and compared with a previous closing high of 74,730.36.
"With the first session closing above 75,000 points, people are still confident with another session to go," Garanti Yatirim Bank's Hasan Soydan said.

Dealers said a recovery in volumes reflected a return of confidence, but Soydan said activity was still limited to speculative trading by a few market participants. "Ultimately you still can't say the wider public has entered the market," he said.
The Turkish market had been held back in recent months by concerns about the Islamist-led government's economic plans.
